cases.reason: DP 0.7 Section 3 and 12 establish that primitive structural correspondence precedes and overrides high-level labels; different labels do not block discovery when the underlying construction matches.

Shared labels do not override primitive structural differences; a cycle is not semantically equivalent to recursion without appropriate authority. The candidate exact match fails the descent to primitive support required by Section 13.1.
DP 0.7 Section 4 explicitly permits multiple valid derived views over the same primitive structure; they do not need to form an exclusive taxonomy.
DP 0.7 Section 7 and 4 allow derived views to preserve complex recurrence topologies, including multiple paths and nesting, without forcing a fixed grammar.
DP 0.7 Section 10 requires preserving unresolved structure through QU; an invariant property (recurrence) can be established across the realization family without inventing a specific count.
Non-scalar unresolved topology must be preserved as QU; DP 0.7 Section 10 forbids collapsing such structure into a scalar or selecting an arbitrary representative.

DP 0.7 Section 6 and 13 establish that derived views are interpretations that cannot substitute for primitive structure in an exact claim; lossy projections must be declared.
DP 0.7 Section 13.1 requires descent to primitive support for exact witness promotion; the candidate fails because the primitive incidence differs despite the common high-level view.
DP 0.7 Section 10 allows establishing invariants that hold across all admissible realizations of a QU family without selecting a specific realization or resolving the unknown shape.
DP 0.7 Section 15 requires routing transition-sensitive comparisons through DTS; state-level similarity does not override load-bearing transition-order differences in an exact correspondence claim.
